registry_info.name: boundary_tank
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `boundary` family's wave-equation dialect (fixed / free / absorbing / periodic). One pulse, one integration, four edge rules, four channels standing side by side.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. The four lane names come from WAVE_SRC.BOUNDARIES at build time and the four moment fractions from SORT_SRC.MOMENTS; do not retype either here or in the script.

boundary_tank.name: Boundary Tank
boundary_tank.description: Four channels stacked on one panel, each running the SAME wave under a different boundary condition. One Gaussian pulse is launched rightward at 3/8 of every lane and integrated ONCE at build time on a 128-cell lattice at Courant number exactly 1, where the leapfrog is exact. Four one-line edge rules are the only difference between the lanes: fixed pins the end at u = 0 and the crest returns INVERTED; free copies the neighbouring cell and it returns upright, one cell early; absorbing takes the Sommerfeld one-way condition, which at r = 1 is exact, and the wave leaves and never comes back; periodic wraps the stencil, so what exits the right end arrives at the left and the tank is secretly a ring. `moment` chooses which moment of one round trip is standing; `evidence` chooses how much of the run is on the table - the water alone, the water with the released pulse ghosted over it and the energy counted, or the whole run strobed at its quarters. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random.
interactions: read the four lanes top to bottom at moment=done: a trough, a crest, an empty channel, and a crest on the wrong side of the tank - one wave, four theories of the outside
put the top two lanes together: same place, opposite sign, and the only difference in the code is u[N] = 0 against u[N] = u[N-1]
switch to moment=quarter and watch the argument disappear - all four lanes are identical until the wave arrives at the end
at moment=half the pinned lane is FLAT and its energy bar is still full: the displacement is zero and every joule is in the velocity
at evidence=longhand read the strobe: fixed crosses the datum, free never does, absorbing stops, periodic runs off one end and in at the other
boundary_tank.capacity: SEE that a boundary condition is a claim about a place the picture does not show, and that it is unfalsifiable from inside the tank until the wave gets there
boundary_tank.qfep_connection: Four accounts of an outside, none of them observable from within. The lanes are bit-identical for eighty of the run's hundred and sixty steps and they are four different worlds the whole time - the difference is real before it is visible, which is the condition of every structure that decides what a system may do at its edge. The artifact's own dark spot is `absorbing`: the lane that draws no wall, keeps no record and ends empty is the one whose claim is largest, because it asserts that the domain continues forever in a direction the exhibit cannot show. It is also the only lane whose energy bar reaches zero, and the only place in the piece where nothing is the correct picture.
boundary_tank.relationships:
Synthesised from [[wave_equation_solver]], which owns the four-value `boundary` vocabulary this tank exhibits, and which can only ever stand in ONE of them at a time because a membrane can only have one rim.

THE WORD IS THREE QUESTIONS AND THE REGISTRY HAS TO SAY SO. Five artifacts declare `boundary` and they carry three unrelated value lists - see dna.kin. This tank takes the wave solver's and names the other two rather than leaving the next agent to discover the split.

[[sorting_hall]] OWNS `moment`. Its const MOMENTS := {start: 0.0, quarter: 0.25, half: 0.5, done: 1.0} is preloaded and read, not copied, so the two synthesis shells cannot drift into two ladders. Its PANEL_COLOR is reused for the same reason: the two shells should photograph as siblings.

[[wave_interference_tank]] and [[wave_interference_3d]] own `evidence` in this corner of the corpus. Their static evidence_name() is the reader an evidence token is routed through here, exactly as the 3D twin routes its own, so `pattern`, `field`, `section` and `terms` cannot mean different rungs in three artifacts.

[[noise_quarry]] is the construction precedent: one field, evaluated once, cut N ways, with the family word exhibited rather than swept. [[removal_room]] is the same move for `removal`. This tank is that pattern applied to a family whose values are not three drawings of one object but four different simulations.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: A flat panel 2.70 m wide, 2.206 m tall and 0.096 m deep, standing with its base at y = 0, so the grid's base-to-floor grounding is a no-op and no auto_ground opt-out is needed. It is read from the front (+Z); `wall_backing` is true because the artifact BRINGS its own panel and should not be given a second wall 0.4 m behind it. There is no collider anywhere in the file, so the pathfinder will route straight through it - correct, because it is a picture.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry and re-derived in a Python replica of the same constants; no Godot was run, per the brief. Everything drawn is one of TWO MeshInstance3D (a shaded SurfaceTool mesh and an unshaded one for the water), so the capture AABB is exactly the union and no `layers = 0` anchor is needed or present. X = MARGIN_L 0.28 + LANE_X 2.24 + MARGIN_R 0.18. Y = HEADER 0.10 + 0.03 + 4 x BAND 0.49 + 3 x GAP 0.032 + 0.02. Z = the panel slab back at -0.030 to the strobe front at +0.066. The five Label3D (four lane names and the header) are not MeshInstance3D and do not enter the box.

dna.axis_shape:
THE EXHIBITED WORD IS PARALLEL; BOTH AXES NEST. Answered from the owner's code, not from its prose.

`boundary` sits SIDE BY SIDE. wave_equation_solver._step_wave branches four ways and no branch contains another: `periodic` returns early into an entirely separate loop because the wrap is in the stencil and cannot be expressed as an edge treatment after an interior sweep; `free` calls _apply_free_edges on the new level; `absorbing` calls _apply_sponge on BOTH leapfrog levels; `fixed` does nothing, the interior-only range having already left the rim at zero. The furniture says it twice - four builders (_build_frame_fixed / _free / _absorbing / _periodic) sharing no body. Parallel values are exactly the case in which showing them all at once is NOT merely the top value, so the word is exhibited as four standing lanes and the axes vary the run.

`evidence` nests in the ordinary way: result is contained in trace is contained in longhand. _build() adds the datum rule, the two amplitude rules, the energy gauge and strobe station 0 under `if evidence != "result"`, and stations 1-4 under `evidence == "longhand"`. No rung removes a mark an earlier rung drew and the four lanes are identical at all three.

`moment` nests as a fraction of one run, which is sorting_hall's own reading of the word: 0.0 is contained in 0.25 is contained in 0.5 is contained in 1.0, as a prefix of the same integration. Nothing is recomputed between rungs - _run() fills all 162 frames once and every rung indexes into them.
dna.default:
evidence=longhand, moment=done.

A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the preservation rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of PLACED artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom is spent on the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest.

WHY `done` AND NOT `half`. Measured, not preferred. At `done` the four lanes read -1.000000 at cell 48, +1.000010 at cell 47, nothing at all, and +1.000020 at cell 80 - four full-amplitude marks in four different places or signs, and the only moment at which all four claims are simultaneously at full strength. `half` is the more dramatic instant and the weaker photograph: the fixed lane is FLAT there (max |u| = 9.93e-06, exact cancellation of the incident pulse against its own inverted image) and the absorbing lane is half gone, so two of the four lanes are nearly empty at once. `start` and `quarter` are the two moments at which the exhibit's whole subject is invisible, which is the artifact's first claim and a poor front door.

WHY `longhand` AND NOT `result`. `result` is four water lobes and no way to say they came from one release - a picture of four sculptures rather than of an argument. `longhand` strobes the whole run at its quarters, and it is the only rung at which a single frame carries the finding without a caption: the fixed lane's strobe crosses the datum, the free lane's never does, the absorbing lane's stops halfway across, and the periodic lane's runs off one end and in at the other.

DECLARATION ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. build_dna_gallery.sweep walks the axes in declaration order and trims the LATER one from the TAIL until the cross product fits the cap. `evidence` is first and is never trimmed. `moment` is declared done, half, quarter, start rather than in time order, so that at the gallery's default --max=9 the 3 x 4 renders as evidence(3) x moment(2) = [done, half] - the two moments at which the four lanes differ at all - instead of dropping them and measuring the axis on the two frames where nothing has happened yet. THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=12.
dna.was: nothing. This artifact did not exist before this pass. It is the cross-lane comparison wave_equation_solver's own registry describes from inside one value of it - `the equation u_tt = c2 grad2 u is identical on a drumhead, on an open pond, in an anechoic tank and on a torus; the thing that distinguishes them is the BOUNDARY CONDITION` - built as a body. Measured, not assumed: a sweep of every registry file returns exactly 5 entries declaring `boundary`, and they carry THREE different value lists.
dna.kin:
THE WORD IS THREE QUESTIONS. `boundary` is declared by five artifacts in three unrelated vocabularies, and the registry has to say so rather than let the next agent find out by colliding with it:

  (a) none | edge | cell | lattice - vr_tile_editor, vr_tile_editor_mirror, pattern_maker_station. AN EDITOR'S SNAP TARGET: what a drawn stroke is rounded to. The subject is a cursor and the values are quantisers.
  (b) fixed | free | absorbing | periodic - wave_equation_solver. THE BOUNDARY CONDITION OF A WAVE EQUATION. The subject is a domain and the values are what happens at its edge.
  (c) flow | cage | corners | open - force_field_zone. WHAT A ZONE DOES TO A BODY ENTERING IT, i.e. a containment policy. The subject is a volume and the values are its manners.

THIS TANK TAKES (b), AND THE REASON IS NOT THAT IT IS THE BIGGEST GROUP - it is the smallest, one artifact against three. It is taken because it is the only one of the three whose values describe a BOUNDARY. (a) names a snap rule, which is a property of an editor and not of an edge; (c) names a containment policy, which is a property of a zone's interior. Only (b) answers the question `what happens where the domain stops`, and its four words - fixed, free, absorbing, periodic - are the standard boundary conditions of the wave equation, which is the mathematics this corpus is teaching. Taking (a) or (c) here would be taking a word and giving it a different answer, which is the folding_past fault.

THE LIST IS PRELOADED, NOT RETYPED. boundary_tank.gd opens with
  const WAVE_SRC := preload("res://commons/artifacts/wave_equation_solver/wave_equation_solver.gd")
and the lanes, their number and their order come from WAVE_SRC.BOUNDARIES at build time. wave_equation_solver was chosen over the other four because it is the one that HAS the const - the other four carry the word only in an @export_enum hint, which cannot be read from another script. _check_family_lists() runs at _ready and push_errors in BOTH directions: a value the solver declares that this tank has no lane for, and a lane this tank builds that the solver has dropped. That check exists because passing tools/check_dna_declarations.py is not evidence the vocabulary agrees - that gate reads @export_enum hints out of the source TEXT without parsing anything.

`moment` IS SORTING_HALL'S WORD AND ITS FRACTIONS. Two artifacts declare `moment` and they disagree: sorting_hall says start | quarter | half | done and laser_exploding_sphere says intact | fissured | burst | scattered. The second is a ladder of named stages of a one-way destruction and has no reading here (a pulse does not fissure). The first is a FRACTION OF A RUN and it is machine-readable: sorting_hall.gd carries `const MOMENTS: Dictionary = {"start": 0.0, "quarter": 0.25, "half": 0.5, "done": 1.0}`, which this tank preloads and indexes, so the words AND the numbers behind them are the family's. The run here is one round trip - out to the far end and back - and the four fractions land on whole steps by construction, which is why the launch cell is 3/8 of the lane and not a rounder-looking 1/4 (see dna.declines).

`evidence` IS THE WAVE FAMILY'S WORD, TAKEN WITH A SUB-LIST THAT ALREADY EXISTS. 47 registry entries declare `evidence`; 28 carry result | trace | longhand | axiom, four carry result | trace | sources | longhand (wave_interference_tank, wave_interference_3d, force_field_visualizer, DualBallFMController) and EIGHT carry exactly result | trace | longhand, in that order (ftc_bridge, zeno_staircase, sine_wave_controller, generator_bench among them). This takes the three-rung list character for character and refuses `sources` on the record with arithmetic - see dna.declines. A token is routed through WaveInterferenceTank.evidence_name(), the family's one reader, rather than through a second alias table here.
declines: `sources`, THE FOURTH RUNG OF THE WAVE FAMILY'S `evidence`, and this is the one refusal with a number attached. wave_equation_solver's own registry already ruled the word out for this subject - `sources and longhand name the two addends being summed. There are no two addends here: one pulse, one field, nothing being added` - and left a door open for a second axis. The door was tried. The honest `sources` for a boundary problem is the METHOD OF IMAGES: fixed is the incident pulse plus ONE inverted mirror source, free plus one upright one, periodic plus the whole periodic train, and absorbing plus NOTHING, which is precisely the claim that there is no outside. It is the most illuminating rung this artifact could have had and it does not fit, geometrically. At `done` the incident source of the fixed lane stands at cell 48 + 160 = 208, i.e. 80 cells = 1.40 m beyond a wall that is 2.24 m from the other one; drawing it needs a margin 62% as wide as the lane itself and a panel 5.5 m across for one lobe. Cut the margin to something affordable and the extension band is FLAT at three of the four moments, because the images are outside it. Refused, and the refusal is enforced in code: a map token reading #evidence:sources (or `fronts`, which the family's own reader normalises to it) push_warnings and keeps the standing value rather than silently falling through to the default.

THE SPACE-TIME CARPET, designed, built, rasterised and cut - and it is the reason this artifact has a strobe. Each lane was first given an x-t diagram of its own run under the band, the one drawing in which a boundary condition becomes a shape you can see (a wedge for fixed and free, a line that stops for absorbing, a stripe that wraps for periodic). The arithmetic killed it. A lane 2.24 m long can afford a strip about 0.11 m tall before the panel stops fitting the frame, i.e. 445 x 26 px at this framing; the pulse is 25.07 cells wide, so the characteristic crosses 445 px of x while rising 13 px of t and its PERPENDICULAR thickness is 87 x (13/445) = 2.5 px. Rendered, it measured 2.3 px and the whole `longhand` rung came back at 1.66-3.08% focus against `trace` - four twins, on the critic's own bar of 6%. An x-t diagram wants an aspect near 1:1 and this lane is seventeen times wider than the strip can be tall. The whole run is drawn as a STROBE in the profile strip instead, where there is height to draw it in, and the same pair now predicts 27.77-29.12%.

THE PARENT'S SPONGE, and this is a measurement about a shipped artifact rather than about this one. wave_equation_solver implements `absorbing` as a damping layer six cells deep on a 48-cell membrane, tapering to 0.80 per substep, applied to both leapfrog levels. Transposed here at the parent's own floor, its own linear profile and its own fraction of the domain (6/48 x 128 = 16 cells, which is 1.6 pulse-sigmas deep, matching the parent's own 6 cells against its 3.84-cell pulse to within 3%), it leaves 60.5% OF THE AMPLITUDE and 22.3% of the energy in the tank after one round trip, and reflects 39.9% at contact. It does not deliver the answer its own word promises. It does not have to: in 2D there is no exact local absorbing condition and a sponge is the honest approximation. In 1D at Courant number exactly 1 there IS one - the Sommerfeld one-way condition u[N]^{n+1} = u[N-1]^n - and it is exact: measured residual 1.60e-05 of amplitude and 0.000000 of energy at `done`. This tank runs the exact condition, because the word names the condition and not the approximation, and it reports the sponge measurement rather than quietly implying the parent was wrong.

DAMPING. wave_equation_solver ships damping = 0.002 per substep, which over this run would remove 27% of the amplitude in every lane. It is refused and the reason is law 6 rather than taste: the exhibit claims to show what the BOUNDARY does to the wave, so a bulk loss term would put energy loss in all four lanes and turn `absorbing` into a difference of degree. The medium here is lossless, and every joule that leaves has left through an edge. It is also what makes the energy gauge readable at all - fixed, free and periodic sit at exactly 1.000000 at every declared moment, so the absorbing lane's 0.500071 and 0.000000 are unambiguous.

SUM OF SQUARES AS THE ENERGY. Not refused as an axis - refused as a MEASURE, and it is worth recording because it would have shipped a false statement. The obvious gauge for `how much of the wave is left` is sum(u*u), and at moment=half the fixed lane's displacement is zero in every cell (measured max |u| = 9.93e-06, the exact cancellation of the incident pulse against its own inverted image), so that gauge would read 0.000 and the tank would have stated that a pinned wall destroys a wave. It is sorting_hall's fault exactly - a proxy that silently reports zero - one artifact later and in a different costume. _energy() computes the quantity the leapfrog actually conserves, E = 1/2 sum (u^{n+1} - u^n)^2 + 1/2 sum grad(u^n) . grad(u^{n+1}), which reads 1.000000 there because every joule is in the velocity.

ANY ANIMATION, RATE OR DECAY. A wave tank has obvious time-domain axes and every one of them is invisible to a still PNG. There is no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body and no randf/randi/randomize anywhere in the file; _ready runs the integration once and lays the finished panel out in one frame. `moment` is the only time in the artifact and it is a FROZEN INDEX into a precomputed run, not a rate. No dna.fixture is needed and none is declared.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL TWELVE FRAMES, which for this artifact is the panel: the panel, the four channels, the gauge tracks and the end-wall furniture stand at every value of both axes, and the marks the axes add are all inside them. Union box 2.700 x 2.206 x 0.096, diagonal sqrt(7.29 + 4.866436 + 0.009216) = 3.487930, radius 1.743965.

THE RIG: FOV 34, PAD 1.9, dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing = 1.743965 / 0.3057307 x 1.9 x 0.47 = 5.093897 m, so the visible frame at the subject's centre plane is 2 x PAD x radius x framing = 3.114721 m and a 760 px still is 244.00 px per metre.

WHY 0.47 WAS FOUND BY PERSPECTIVE PROJECTION AND NOT BY THE USUAL ORTHOGRAPHIC ESTIMATE. The arithmetic this corpus normally uses - projected extent = |right.x| x W + |right.z| x D with right = (cos 0.62, 0, -sin 0.62) - is orthographic, and it is wrong here by 8%, in the unsafe direction. The camera stands 5.09 m from a body 2.70 m wide, and the view direction (0.5615, 0.2571, 0.7865) has a large x component, so the panel's near end is 1.52 m closer to the camera than its far end and is magnified about 1.34x more. All eight AABB corners were projected through the actual pinhole: the true span is 595.6 x 629.9 px (78.4% x 82.9% of frame) where the orthographic formula predicts 549.8 x 623.5 px (72.3% x 82.0%). The spread is almost entirely in x, which is the axis with the depth component. At framing 0.42, which is roughly what the orthographic estimate recommends, the true span is 675 x 707 px and the corners land at x = 774.7 and y = 773.1 - CLIPPED on two sides by about 14 px, while the orthographic formula reports a comfortable 649 x 649 and nothing in the chain would have said otherwise. 0.47 puts the corners at x [126.8, 722.4] and y [96.7, 726.6]; the tightest margin is 33.4 px, at the BOTTOM, which is the corner nearest the camera.

WHY BELOW 1/PAD = 0.5263, WHICH IS WHERE THE BOUNDING SPHERE STARTS TO BE CROPPED. The body is a slab 0.096 m thick, so its bounding sphere is 96% air; what has to fit is the projected extent, and it does, measured, with margin. Above 0.52 the subject drops under 74% of frame width and the marks lose pixels for nothing.

EVERY MARK WAS GAUGED AT 244.00 px/m BEFORE THE SIZES WERE FIXED (law 4). Verticals use cos(pitch) = 0.966390 and horizontals |right.x| = 0.813878:
  amplitude, u = 1        0.113 m  -> 26.65 px      (free's 1.995 at contact -> 53.16 px)
  pulse width, 2.5066 sig 0.4387 m -> 87.11 px
  datum rule              0.024 m  ->  5.66 px
  amplitude rules, +/-1   0.020 m  ->  4.72 px
  strobe / ghost outline  0.026 m  ->  6.13 px
  energy gauge track      0.030 m  ->  7.07 px tall, 444.8 px long
  fixed clamp bar         0.052 m  -> 10.33 px wide, 108.4 px tall
  free post               0.052 m  -> 10.33 px wide,  54.2 px tall
  periodic strip          0.036 m  ->  7.15 px wide
  absorbing open mouth    0.070 m  -> 13.90 px
  one lattice cell        0.0175 m ->  3.48 px
The thinnest mark is the +/-1 rule at 4.72 px, well clear of the 1-3 px band law 4 exists because of. The critic crops to 584 x 622 px and resizes to 160 x 160, so screen pixels are divided by about 3.7 in both axes and a 4.72 px rule survives as 1.3 samples across 130 samples of length; the amplitude mark survives as 6.9 samples.

FIRST BUILD, FOR THE RECORD: the lane was 224 cells with sigma 6.5, which made the pulse 7.3% of the lane, and the water covered 0.81% of the panel. `moment` measured 1.24-2.20% focus - INERT - and the fault was not the axis but the dilution. The launch was moved to 3/8 of the lane, which is the largest offset that keeps the round trip divisible by four, sigma raised to 10/128 = 7.8% of the lane, and the water made unshaded as wave_equation_solver's own surface material is. `moment` now predicts 13.48%.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency rather than in changed pixels, because a prediction in the wrong units is a prediction about a different instrument. The numbers below come from building this exact geometry in Python from the same constants, running the same four integrations, rasterising with a z-buffer through this exact camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, framing 0.47) and pushing the twelve frames through artifact_dna_critic's pipeline unchanged: crop to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralise each frame's own corner background, greyscale, resize to 160 x 160, mean of the hottest 5%.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS `moment` quarter <-> start, AT evidence=longhand: 9.74% focus, 0.509% frame, on a crop of 584 x 622 px.

WHY THAT PAIR, ARITHMETICALLY, AND IT IS A THREE-PART ANSWER. (1) At `start` and `quarter` all four lanes hold the IDENTICAL field - the pulse has not reached an end, so the four boundary rules have not yet been consulted. Measured: every lane peaks at +1.000000 at cell 48 and at +1.000010 at cell 88 respectively, and the largest disagreement between any two lanes at either moment is 1.0e-05. So the only thing that moves between these two frames is one lobe per lane, 40 cells to the right. (2) The energy gauge, which is the other thing `moment` normally moves, is IDENTICAL at these two moments: E/E0 is 1.000000 for all four lanes at both, because nothing has left yet. (3) And `longhand` is the rung that weakens it further, because the strobe already stands at BOTH positions in both frames - stations 0 and 0.25 are drawn whatever the moment - so the moving lobe is landing on ghost outlines that were there anyway. The same value pair reads 15.70% at `result`, where the lobe moves against a bare channel: a 1.61x context spread, and the reason is that longhand's strobe already occupies the water's destination. Grouped by value pair across contexts, quarter <-> start runs 9.74 / 13.01 / 15.70 - never a twin, and never inert.

FULL PREDICTED SHEET, focus %, at each of the four moments (done / half / quarter / start):
    evidence result <-> trace       26.39  27.70  28.82  27.22
    evidence trace <-> longhand     28.46  28.80  27.77  29.12
    evidence result <-> longhand    39.39  39.80  39.22  39.55
and, at each of the three evidence rungs (result / trace / longhand):
    moment quarter <-> start        15.70  13.01   9.74
    moment done <-> start           10.19  12.31  10.47
    moment done <-> half            14.19  14.65  11.46
    moment done <-> quarter         13.32  15.94  12.74
    moment half <-> start           15.02  14.80  12.72
    moment half <-> quarter         16.43  16.59  13.32
AXIS MEANS: `evidence` 2.269% frame / 31.85% focus -> BITES, comfortably. `moment` 0.715% frame / 13.48% focus -> BITES, by 1.48 points. No pair is under the 6% twin bar and none is under the 3% inert bar; the minimum in the whole sheet is 9.74%.

SUBJECT SHARE, rasterised: 75.8% (result), 77.7% (trace), 76.9% (longhand) at moment=done, against the critic's 6% blank-render floor. The union subject box is IDENTICAL in all twelve frames - (138, 97, 722, 719) - because the panel, the channels and the end-wall furniture stand at every value, so the camera does not move between tiles and the frames are strictly comparable pixel to pixel. That is worth stating because wave_equation_solver's own registry warns that ITS four values change the artifact's footprint, so its own tiles are not.

THE PREDICTION IS A FLOOR, NOT A FORECAST. Measured across the four predictions in this corpus that named a pair and a number, every one under-predicted, by 1.5x to 6.7x, because a Python rasteriser has one directional light, flat shading and no shadows, ambient occlusion or antialiasing. Read 9.74% as a lower bound. THE RULE THAT BUYS: if the sweep comes back BELOW these numbers, something is broken, and the first thing to check is not the design.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT, AND WHAT EACH WOULD MEAN.
(a) If any `evidence` pair reads near 0.00%, run tools/check_dna_declarations.py --token=boundary_tank first: a value the code cannot reach falls back to the default and prints identical tiles.
(b) If `moment` comes back near 0% while `evidence` bites, the run is not being re-indexed - apply_grid_config rebuilds only when a value actually CHANGED and _built is true, so a sweep that sets moment before _ready and again after would be a no-op the second time and correct the first.
(c) If `moment` lands ABOVE `evidence`, the strobe is not drawing: at `longhand` the strobe is 80% of what separates the rungs, and without it `moment`'s marks would be moving against bare channels at every rung.
(d) The replica does not model the five Label3D. They are constant in all twelve tiles and add roughly 0.4% more constant subject area to every crop, which dilutes both axis means slightly - so these numbers are a little high, not a little low, in that one respect.
(e) The replica renders the water with |n.L| = 1 (unshaded, as the artifact's own material is) and everything else with a single Lambert term and no shadows. In Godot the shaded faces pointing away from the showcase key will go darker than the replica draws them, which affects the constant furniture more than the marks.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a number is read correctly.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF BOTH AXES: the panel, the header, the four channel wells, the five Label3D, and all eight pieces of end-wall furniture. The furniture is the one large constant and it is deliberate - it is what makes each lane's condition legible when the wave is nowhere near it. Four brown clamps, four brown half-height posts, two open mouths and four cyan strips: 3.4% of the panel's face.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `evidence`: the water. All three rungs run the identical integration and photograph the identical field; what changes is what is standing around it.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `moment`: the strobe, at `longhand`. This is a design decision and it is the opposite of the obvious one. A strobe that grew with the moment would be empty at `start` - and `start` is already the moment at which the four lanes are identical, so the two thin things would have compounded and `trace` <-> `longhand` at `start` would have been a twin. Drawing the whole run at every moment costs `moment` some of its bite at `longhand` (13.32% down to 9.74% on its thinnest pair) and buys `evidence` a rung that is equally strong everywhere. The trade is recorded rather than hidden.

THE FOUR LANES ARE IDENTICAL AT TWO OF THE FOUR MOMENTS, TO 1.0e-05, AND THIS IS NOT A FAULT. It is the artifact's first claim: a boundary condition is unfalsifiable from inside the tank until the wave reaches the edge. Eighty of the run's hundred and sixty steps produce four bit-identical pictures of four different worlds. Do not 'fix' it by launching the pulse nearer the wall - that would trade the claim for pixels, and it would also break the moment fractions, which land on whole steps only because the launch is at 3/8 of the lane.

THE FIXED LANE IS FLAT AT `half`, AND ITS ENERGY BAR IS FULL. Max |u| = 9.93e-06 across the whole lane, E/E0 = 1.000000. That is the exact cancellation of the incident pulse against its own inverted image at the instant the centre reaches the wall, and it is the single most falsifiable thing in the piece: if that lane is not flat at `half`, the Dirichlet edge is not being applied, and if its bar is not full, _energy has been replaced by a sum of squares.

THE FREE LANE COMES BACK ONE CELL EARLY, AND THAT IS THE DISCRETE CONDITION SPEAKING. At `done` the fixed lane's trough sits at cell 48 and is the EXACT negative of the released pulse (max |u_start + u_done| = 9.93e-06), because the Dirichlet surface is exactly at the sample. The free lane's crest sits at cell 47, and max |u_start - u_done| = 0.060466 against |g'|max = exp(-0.5)/sigma = 0.060653 - the entire discrepancy is one cell of shift, to 0.3%, because the discrete Neumann condition puts the reflecting surface half a cell outside the sample. Two conditions that are textbook mirror images of each other are not mirror images on a lattice, and the tank shows it without being asked.

FREE'S ENERGY OVERSHOOTS ITS OWN CEILING BY 0.22% AT `half` (E/E0 = 1.002223) because the discrete Neumann condition is not exactly energy conserving. The gauge clamps at 1.000, which costs 1.0 px of a 445 px bar. Reported rather than papered over.

NO TEXT NAMES AN AXIS VALUE. There are five Label3D and they letter the header word `boundary` and the four lane names, all of which stand at every value of both axes. Not one pixel of any tile is a rendered word naming its own variant. Billboard is disabled on all five, which also keeps LabelFramer from bolting a panel and a bezel behind each one.

THE Z-STACK, WRITTEN OUT, because operations_gallery's bezel was a slab in front of every mark it was supposed to frame. Six layers, back to front: panel slab -0.030 to 0.000; channel wells and the absorbing mouths 0.000 to 0.004; rules, gauge track and gauge fill 0.004 to 0.010; the water 0.010 to 0.054; end-wall furniture 0.004 to 0.060; the strobe 0.054 to 0.066. THE STROBE IS DELIBERATELY IN FRONT OF THE WATER, by 12 mm, because at `start` and at `done` the solid water sits exactly on a strobe station in three of the four lanes and an outline behind it would vanish at precisely the moments it is making its point. It is an OUTLINE 26 mm thick, not a fill, so it occludes 6.13 px of a lobe that is 87 px wide. Nothing else overlaps: the furniture stands at the lane ends where no mark is drawn, and the rules are behind the water on purpose - the water sits on its own datum.

STAGING. The panel is 2.70 m, under the 6 m cut-off, so a --staged run would put a plinth under it, grow the pair AABB and shrink every mark. The numbers above are for an unstaged sweep.
